title: cross-pillar-reliability-cadence-and-slo-triage-template-initiative
body:
Purpose
This note captures a proposed cross-pillar reliability cadence and a lightweight SLO triage template that platform, serving-runtime, product, and SRE can pilot over a 12-week lab. Aim: create a repeatable handoff pattern for SLO definition, operationalization, and emergency triage that reduces time-to-resolution and clarifies escalation flows.

Audience
- Platform Engineering leads
- Site Reliability Engineering
- Serving Runtime owners
- Product and Console PMs
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success (for customer-impact scenarios)

Context / Background
We have many ad-hoc SLO conversations across teams. Recent incidents highlighted ambiguity in who owns mitigation vs model-level rollbacks, and capacity simulation results are not consistently captured. This doc proposes a pragmatic cadence, decision triggers, and a triage template to standardize cross-team responses and to accelerate SLO onboarding for new services (including model-serving endpoints).

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO breaches by 30% in pilot teams within 12 weeks.
- Standardize SLO metadata capture (owner, measurement query, alert threshold, fallback policy) for 90% of services onboarded in the pilot.
- Create an SLO triage template used in 100% of post-incident runbooks for category A or B breaches during the pilot.

Phased plan
Phase 0: Align (wk 0–1)
- Kickoff with leads: clarify scope and success metrics.
- Inventory: quick audit of top 25 model-serving routes and critical platform services.
- Output: baseline MTTA/MTTR metrics and inventory table (owner, current alert, measurement source).

Phase 1: Design + Templates (wk 2–3)
- Draft SLO metadata schema (single-row friendly for sheets).
- Draft SLO triage template (see below).
- Run two hour design workshop with product and SRE to validate fallbacks and customer-impact taxonomy.

Phase 2: Pilot (wk 4–9)
- Select 4 pilot services spanning hosted API, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Implement SLO metadata and wire alerts into shared incident dashboard.
- Run weekly triage tabletop for simulated degradations (latency spike, token error surge, KV cache corruption).

Phase 3: Iterate + Rollout (wk 10–12)
- Analyze pilot metrics, capture runbooks, update triage template.
- Publish lightweight handbook + checklist to Confluence.
- Plan next cohort onboarding cadence and training schedule.

Deliverables
- SLO metadata spreadsheet (single row per SLO): service, route, owner, prometheus query/trace source, alert threshold, SLO target, fallback policy, rollback owner, downstream stakeholders.
- Triage template + sample filled runbooks for three incident archetypes.
- Weekly cross-pillar cadence schedule and meeting materials.
- Post-pilot retrospective and playbook with rollout recommendations.

Proposed SLO triage template (fill at first alert)
- Incident id / start time:
- SLO breached: (name + target)
- Signal / symptom: (latency / errors / quality regression / capacity)
- Initial severity (P1/P2/P3) with rationale:
- Owner (service on-call) and cross-pillar lead present:
- Immediate mitigation actions taken (who did what, timestamp):
  * throttle routes / degrade to cached responses / switch region / pin model variant
- Checkpoints (5m, 15m, 60m): observed signal, actions, decision (roll forward / rollback / escalate), next checkpoint owner
- Customer impact note: (affected customers, likely exposure)
- If rollback decision: rollback owner, rollback window, verification queries
- If capacity/fallback used: capacity stage invoked, runbook link
- Postmortem action items and owner (one-line for each)

Cadence & meetings (suggested)
- Weekly Reliability Sync (30m): cross-pillar owners; review ongoing degradations, outstanding runbook gaps, and next experiments.
- SLO Onboarding Workshop (bi-weekly 60m): hands-on for new services, fill SLO metadata row, and validate fallback.
- Monthly Capacity Tabletop (90m): simulate capacity and region-fallback scenarios with product/customer success present.
- Incident Triage Handoff (ad-hoc): use the triage template; SRE chairs until handoff to platform/product owner is clear.

Roles & responsibilities (high level)
- Service owner (typically product/serving runtime): defines SLO target and acceptance criteria; implements measurement.
- SRE: validates measurement, builds alerting, and owns initial triage and escalation ladder.
- Platform: provides capacity simulations, rollout policies, and emergency routing changes.
- Solutions Eng / CS: owns customer comms playbook and provides impact estimates.
- Reliability Program Lead (rotating): runs cadence, collects metrics, and drives retro.

Capacity scenarios to capture (minimum)
- Normal: 95th latency within target at baseline traffic.
- Gradual degradation: error rate growth over 60m due to memory leak/kv evictions.
- Burst overload: sudden 3x traffic for 10–30m (simulate through load generator).
- Regional outage: primary region down, failover to secondary with 20% higher latency.
- Model-quality regression: automated eval score drop causing increased retries and throttle.

Templates & artefacts (links to create)
- SLO metadata sheet (template tab) -> confluence link placeholder
- Incident triage playbook (markdown) -> github link placeholder
- Rollout rollback checklist -> confluence page

Risk matrix (quick)
- Risk: ambiguous ownership -> Mitigation: make owner required field in SLO metadata, validate at onboarding workshop.
- Risk: alert fatigue / noisy signals -> Mitigation: introduce burn-in period and alert tuning window during pilot.
- Risk: platform capacity mismatch -> Mitigation: pre-flight capacity sims and documented emergency scaling steps.

Communication plan
- When an SLO breach impacts customers: CS drafts message within 30m (template in playbook).
- Internal comms: incident channel created in Slack with standard prefix [RELIABILITY-INCIDENT].
- Weekly summary: short CSV of breaches + MTTA/MTTR posted to #reliability-weekly.

Quick checklist for first 90 days
- [ ] Kickoff with all pillar leads and secure time for weekly syncs.
- [ ] Complete inventory of top 25 routes + owners.
- [ ] Run first SLO onboarding workshop for 4 pilot services.
- [ ] Configure triage template as incident runbook in github/confluence.
- [ ] Run two capacity tabletop exercises.
- [ ] Post-pilot retro and publish playbook.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Should we require a single uniform SLO time-window (30d vs 7d) for platform-level services? (tradeoff doc needed).
- How do we surface model-quality SLOs differently from latency/error SLOs (new taxonomy)?
- What is the SLA for CS customer notifications on partial-impact incidents?

Next steps (owners assigned)
- Maya: schedule kickoff + prepare inventory template (due 2026-11-12).
- Liam: draft SLO metadata schema and alert examples (due 2026-11-17).
- Priya: schedule pilot service onboarding and coordinate with CS for tabletop (due 2026-11-19).
- Diego: create initial incident triage markdown and push to github (PR target 2026-11-18).

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep templates intentionally minimal; overhead kills adoption.
- Emphasize rollback owner in every SLO row — previous incidents show this is the gap.
- Consider adding a short e2e test that runs during deploy to validate key SLO queries.

References & links
- Confluence: Reliability program overview (placeholder id above).
- Jira: REL-1234 (pilot cohort tickets).
- GitHub: ops-templates PR to land triage runbook.

-- end of doc --
